ai.text:
The European Parliament approved a regulation, by 558 votes to 93 with 18 abstentions, that creates a free, multilingual online system for companies to declare when they send workers to work in another EU country. The system is linked to the existing Internal Market Information System. Its aims are to make it easier for service providers to operate across borders, cut down on paperwork, and help national authorities check that rules protecting posted workers are followed.

Service providers can use the system to set up a secure account, create and submit posting declarations, check and manage their details, and upload supporting documents once a declaration has been submitted. Every change made by a user is recorded. Workers receive an electronic copy of the parts of the declaration that concern them, along with a link to the official national website giving information on pay and working conditions. The authorities of the host country and the company's home country can see the submitted information and exchange messages with service providers.

Member States that choose to use the system must tell the Commission at least six months in advance. They may not add extra requirements for companies that file through it. Where national law requires it, the system can also accept declarations from companies based outside the EU that send workers into a Member State, so that those firms are not treated more favourably than EU-based ones.

The online form asks for information needed for workplace inspections. This covers the service provider and its legal representative, the posted workers and their number, tasks and indicative hourly pay, the details of the assignment such as dates, type of work, working conditions and any shared accommodation, contact people in the host country and the social partners, and the client receiving the service. For non-EU workers, it also asks for their residence and work permits, or other proof of lawful stay or employment, and the start and, if relevant, end dates of their employment.

The Commission is treated as the controller of the personal data. Information and documents must be kept in the system for up to 36 months after the posting ends, so they can be reused in later declarations. The European Labour Authority will receive statistics drawn from the declarations submitted.
